mechanisms.description: In Effects of Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (ACCORD BP), baseline sbp may modify treatment response through differential baseline cardiovascular risk.
Patients with different sbp levels may show heterogeneous benefit due to variation in baseline disease burden.
Differences in sbp may alter event risk trajectories, changing absolute treatment benefit.
The association between sbp and outcome may interact with treatment intensity in the trial population.
Variation in sbp may identify subgroups with different competing-risk profiles under treatment.
Trial abstract context suggests sbp could act as an effect modifier for clinical outcomes.
